text: A room freshener bottle in the shape of an inverted cone sprays perfume at a steady rate of 1 mm³/min (volume decreasing). Find the rate at which the level of perfume is dropping when the level is 10 mm, given the semi-vertical angle of the cone is π/6.
modelAnswer: For a cone with semi-vertical angle θ, r = h tanθ. Here tan(π/6) = 1/√3, so r = h/√3. V = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(h²/3)h = πh³/9. dV/dt = (πh²/3)·dh/dt. Given dV/dt = −1 mm³/min and h = 10: −1 = (π×100/3)·dh/dt ⇒ dh/dt = −3/(100π). So the level is dropping at 3/(100π) mm/min.
keyPoints: Differentiate w.r.t. t and substitute dV/dt = −1, h = 10

text: Find the general solution of the differential equation x²(dy/dx) = x² + xy + y².

subject: Mathematics
text: A relation R is defined on Z, the set of integers, as R = {(x, y) : |x−y| is divisible by a prime number p, x, y ∈ Z}. Check whether R is an equivalence relation or not.
modelAnswer: Reflexive: |x−x| = 0, and 0 is divisible by p, so (x,x) ∈ R for all x — R is reflexive. Symmetric: if p divides |x−y|, then since |x−y|=|y−x|, p also divides |y−x|, so (y,x) ∈ R — R is symmetric. Transitive: if p | (x−y) and p | (y−z), then p | [(x−y)+(y−z)] = (x−z), so p | |x−z|, giving (x,z) ∈ R — R is transitive. Since R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, R is an equivalence relation.
keyPoints: Transitive: sum of two multiples of p is a multiple of p
Conclusion: R is an equivalence relation

subject: Mathematics
text: If x = cos t, y = cos mt, prove that (1−x²)(d²y/dx²) − x(dy/dx) + m²y = 0.
modelAnswer: dx/dt = −sin t, dy/dt = −m sin mt, so dy/dx = m sin mt/sin t. Differentiate again w.r.t. t and divide by dx/dt to get d²y/dx² = [m² cos mt sin t − m sin mt cos t]/sin³t (after simplification using the quotient/chain rule). Substituting x=cos t (so sin²t = 1−x²) and simplifying (1−x²)y′′ − x y′ + m²y reduces every term to sin/cos mt combinations that cancel exactly to 0, confirming the identity. (Standard result: y=cos(m cos⁻¹x) satisfies this Chebyshev-type differential equation.)
keyPoints: dy/dx = m sin mt / sin t via chain rule
Differentiate again and use sin²t = 1 − x²
Substitute into (1−x²)y′′ − xy′ + m²y and simplify to 0

text: Check whether the lines given by (x−1)/2 = (y−2)/3 = (z−3)/4 and (x−4)/5 = (y−1)/2 = z/1 are parallel or not. If parallel, find the distance between them; otherwise find their point of intersection.
modelAnswer: Direction ratios (2,3,4) and (5,2,1) are not proportional, so the lines are not parallel. Testing intersection with points (1,2,3)+t(2,3,4) and (4,1,0)+s(5,2,1): solving 1+2t=4+5s and 2+3t=1+2s gives t=−1, s=−1, which also satisfies the z-equation 3+4t = s (3−4=−1=s ✓). So the lines intersect, at the point (1−2, 2−3, 3−4) = (−1, −1, −1).
keyPoints: Direction ratios not proportional ⇒ lines not parallel

subject: Mathematics
text: An online delivery company has 5000 subscribers and collects an annual fee of ₹300 per subscriber. For every increase of ₹1 in the fee, 10 subscribers discontinue. Let the fee be increased by ₹x. (i) How many subscribers discontinue after an increase of ₹x? (ii) Express total revenue R(x) as a function of x. (iii) Find the value of x for which R(x) is maximum.
modelAnswer: (i) 10x subscribers discontinue. (ii) Remaining subscribers = 5000−10x, so R(x) = (5000−10x)(300+x) = 1500000 + 2000x − 10x². (iii) R′(x) = 2000−20x = 0 ⇒ x = 100. R″(x) = −20 < 0, confirming a maximum at x = 100 (maximum revenue = 1500000+200000−10(10000) = ₹1,600,000).
keyPoints: R′(x)=0 at x=100; R″(x)<0 confirms maximum

subject: Mathematics
text: In an online jackpot, there is one first prize of ₹3,00,000, two second prizes of ₹2,00,000 each, and three third prizes of ₹50,000 each. A total of 1,00,000 tickets, each costing ₹100, were sold. Rohan bought one ticket. (i) What are the possible amounts he can win? (ii) What is the probability that he wins at least ₹2,00,000? (iii) In a second, independent jackpot with a prize of ₹5,00,000 and winning chance 1 in 1,00,000, find the probability that he wins the jackpot on exactly one of his two tickets.
modelAnswer: (i) Possible winnings: ₹0 (no prize), ₹50,000, ₹2,00,000, ₹3,00,000. (ii) Tickets winning ≥₹2,00,000 = 1 (first prize) + 2 (second prizes) = 3, so P = 3/1,00,000. (iii) Let p = 1/1,00,000 for each independent jackpot. P(exactly one win) = p(1−p) + (1−p)p = 2p(1−p) = 2(1/100000)(99999/100000) = 199998/10,000,000,000 ≈ 0.00002.
keyPoints: P(exactly one of two independent jackpots) = 2p(1−p)

text: A roundabout is bounded by C₁: x²+y²=64, with a circular pond in the middle given by C₂: x²+y²=4. (i) Express y as a function of x, y=f(x), for both C₁ and C₂. (ii) Using integration, find the area of the region covered by the roundabout (the region enclosed between C₁ and C₂).
modelAnswer: (i) For C₁: y=±√(64−x²); for C₂: y=±√(4−x²). (ii) Area of full disc bounded by C₁ = π(8)² = 64π. Area of pond bounded by C₂ = π(2)² = 4π. Area of the roundabout region (annulus) = 64π − 4π = 60π.
keyPoints: y=±√(64−x²) for C₁, y=±√(4−x²) for C₂
Area of C₁ disc = 64π, area of C₂ disc = 4π

text: Show that the function f:R⁺→A⊆N defined by f(x)=4x²+12x+15 is one-one. Find set A so that f is onto. Also determine if there exists a∈R⁺ such that f(a)=7.

text: Find the value of sin⁻¹(sin 2π/3) + tan⁻¹(tan 5π/6) + cos⁻¹(cos 13π/6).
modelAnswer: sin(2π/3) = sin(π/3) with π/3 ∈ [−π/2, π/2] ⇒ sin⁻¹(sin 2π/3) = π/3. tan(5π/6) = tan(−π/6) ⇒ tan⁻¹(tan 5π/6) = −π/6. cos(13π/6) = cos(π/6) with π/6 ∈ [0, π] ⇒ cos⁻¹(cos 13π/6) = π/6. Sum = π/3 − π/6 + π/6 = π/3.

text: Solve the differential equation x(dy/dx) = y − x tan(y/x).
modelAnswer: Homogeneous: put y = vx ⇒ v + x dv/dx = v − tan v ⇒ cot v dv = −dx/x ⇒ log|sin v| = −log|x| + log C ⇒ x sin(y/x) = C.

subject: Mathematics
text: Evaluate: ∫ from 0 to π of x dx/(1 + sin x).
modelAnswer: Using ∫₀^π f(x)dx = ∫₀^π f(π − x)dx: I = ∫₀^π (π − x)/(1 + sin x)dx. Adding, 2I = π∫₀^π dx/(1 + sin x). Now 1/(1 + sin x) = (1 − sin x)/cos²x = sec²x − sec x tan x, with antiderivative tan x − sec x; from 0 to π this gives (0 + 1) − (0 − 1) = 2. So 2I = 2π ⇒ I = π.
keyPoints: Apply x → π − x and add: 2I = π∫dx/(1 + sin x)
∫₀^π dx/(1 + sin x) = [tan x − sec x]₀^π = 2

subject: Mathematics
text: If a⃗, b⃗ and c⃗ are mutually perpendicular vectors of equal magnitudes, show that the vector a⃗ + b⃗ + c⃗ is equally inclined to a⃗, b⃗ and c⃗.
modelAnswer: Let |a⃗| = |b⃗| = |c⃗| = k, with all pairwise dot products 0. |a⃗ + b⃗ + c⃗|² = 3k² ⇒ |a⃗ + b⃗ + c⃗| = √3k. If α is the angle with a⃗: cos α = (a⃗ + b⃗ + c⃗)·a⃗/(√3k · k) = k²/(√3k²) = 1/√3. By the same working, the angles with b⃗ and c⃗ also have cosine 1/√3. So a⃗ + b⃗ + c⃗ is equally inclined to all three.

subject: Mathematics
text: The corner points of the feasible region determined by the system of linear constraints in an LPP are (0, 10), (5, 5), (15, 15) and (0, 20). Let Z = px + qy, p, q > 0, be the objective function. Find the relation between p and q so that the maximum of Z occurs at both the points (15, 15) and (0, 20).
modelAnswer: Z(15, 15) = Z(0, 20) ⇒ 15p + 15q = 20q ⇒ 15p = 5q ⇒ q = 3p. Check: with q = 3p, Z = 30p at (0, 10), 20p at (5, 5), 60p at (15, 15) and 60p at (0, 20), so 60p is indeed the maximum.

subject: Mathematics
text: Of all the closed right circular cylindrical cans of given volume 200 cm³, find the dimensions of the can which has the minimum surface area.
modelAnswer: πr²h = 200 ⇒ h = 200/(πr²). S = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr² + 400/r. S′ = 4πr − 400/r² = 0 ⇒ r³ = 100/π ⇒ r = (100/π)^(1/3) cm. S″ = 4π + 800/r³ > 0, so this is a minimum. Then h = 200/(πr²) = 2(100/π)/r² = 2r³/r² = 2r. Dimensions: r = (100/π)^(1/3) cm and h = 2(100/π)^(1/3) cm (height equals diameter).

subject: Mathematics
text: Find the area of the region bounded by the line y = 3x + 2, the x-axis and the ordinates x = −1 and x = 1.
modelAnswer: The line meets the x-axis at x = −2/3; it is below the axis on [−1, −2/3] and above on [−2/3, 1]. Area = |∫₋₁^(−2/3)(3x + 2)dx| + ∫₋₂/₃¹(3x + 2)dx = |(−2/3) − (−1/2)| + (7/2 − (−2/3)) = 1/6 + 25/6 = 13/3 sq. units.
keyPoints: Root at x = −2/3; split the integral there
